# Swyms

> Swyms (swyms.swymble.com) is a single-screen web toy: a small world of
> one-eyed creatures called Swyms, each generated from a weighted genome.
> Drag them, poke them, and watch them wander, greet each other, play,
> yawn and fall asleep.

The site has two tabs. **World** is the live canvas — four Swyms with
springy bodies, saccadic gaze, blinks, winks and expressions that pass
between them; annoy one and its neighbours startle. **Genome** is the
catalogue: every allele for eye shape, pupil, palette and finish, with
its real drawn thumbnail, its rarity tier and its weight, plus a roller
that mints a new Swym and prints its code and odds.

Rarity is not a lookup table — a trait is rare because its allele is
rare, which is what makes the same weights usable for inheritance later.

Everything runs client-side on one canvas. No accounts, no network calls,
no tracking.

Swyms is part of SWYMBLE Labs, the experiments arm of the SWYMBLE
software studio.
